area.title: Notification record, persistence and publishing
area.scope: The stored notification behind every page: its fields and validation, status values and reference format, create, save and submit, fulfilment and reference-number reads, hard delete, expiry and the admin guard, what is persisted, the outbox events and GBN-AG payload published on submit, and what reaches PIMS Dynamics. Stops at amend, cancel-amend, copy and soft delete (manage-notifications) and at the list API (notification-list). Includes the high-risk plants ledger's rulings on the reference, status lifecycle and data retention.

sources.role: the owner's decisions: outranks every other source. Search boxes use the real frontend's accessible component with MDM's entries. JavaScript behaviour follows the toolbox rule with graceful degradation; JavaScript-only prototype behaviour, pop-ups included, waits on design in its own theme. Commodity catalogue and search wait on MDM; transporter management waits on requirements; the INS dashboard's summary information waits on its requirements. The overview, review, declaration and confirmation are set-owned, and shared parts change add-only. Where plants has the same page or behaviour, the same increment changes it. Each notification list is reframed in its own frontend. The report groups work as ready or blocked. Claims marked as the orchestrator's apply Sam's principles and are not his rulings; ruling:sam-2026-10-09-templates covers templates and the dashboard narrowing.

claims.statement: A notification is stored as one document in the MongoDB collection named "notification".
claims.quote: @org.springframework.data.mongodb.core.mapping.Document(collection = "notification")

claims.statement: The stored notification holds its identity and metadata at the top level and its content (parties, commodity, transport and so on) as a nested notification sub-object, beside a separate fulfilments payload.
claims.quote: Aggregate root: identity + metadata at the top, with the well-structured content held as a composed {@link Notification} sub-object (symmetric with the opaque {@link #fulfilments} payload).

claims.statement: Each stored notification has a string id as its database identity.
claims.quote:
@Id
    private String id;

claims.statement: A notification's reference number is unique across all notifications, and the unique index is sparse, so notifications without a reference number are allowed and do not clash with each other.
claims.quote:
@Indexed(unique = true, sparse = true)
    private String referenceNumber;

claims.statement: Each notification carries a concurrencyToken that is the record's optimistic-locking version number.
claims.quote:
@Version
    private Long concurrencyToken;

claims.statement: Each notification carries a status, one of the NotificationStatus values.
claims.quote: private NotificationStatus status;

claims.statement: Each notification records when it was created and when it was last updated, as instants (moments in time), stamped by the server.
claims.quote:
private Instant created;

    private Instant updated;

claims.statement: A client cannot set a notification's created or updated time: the request shape has no such fields and the server would discard them.
claims.quote: the aggregate's server-stamped {@code created}/{@code updated} instants are deliberately absent here; a client cannot set them and the server would discard them.

claims.statement: Each notification records submittedAt, the time of its most recent submission: set the first time it is submitted from DRAFT and refreshed whenever it is re-submitted from AMEND.
claims.quote: Timestamp of the most recent submission — set the first time the notification is submitted (from DRAFT) and refreshed whenever it is re-submitted from AMEND.

claims.statement: Starting an amendment or cancelling one leaves submittedAt unchanged, so it always points at the latest submission rather than the original one.
claims.quote: Left unchanged by amend and cancel-amend, so it always points at the latest submission event rather than the original one. Set by {@code submitNotification}; carried into the fulfilment-view projection.

claims.statement: A notification created through the app in a non-production environment carries an expiry time (expireAt), anchored to its created time, after which it becomes eligible for automatic expiry.
claims.quote: When this notification becomes eligible for automatic expiry, anchored to {@code created}. Set only for app-created notifications in non-prod environments

claims.statement: In production, and for notifications created before the expiry field existed, a notification has no expiry time.
claims.quote: {@code null} in prod and for notifications created before this field existed.

claims.statement: Expiry is driven by a sweep over a plain index rather than a database TTL index, so expiring a notification can also remove its accompanying documents.
claims.quote: Backed by a plain index (not a Mongo TTL index) so the expiry sweep can cascade to accompanying documents.

claims.statement: The expiry time is never shown in any JSON response.
Each notification stores a fulfilments payload (a list of documents recording obligation fulfilment) exactly as sent, byte for byte; the backend never interprets it.
claims.quote: Opaque obligation-fulfilment payload — persisted byte-faithfully; never interpreted by the backend.

claims.statement: When an amendment starts, the notification's content is snapshotted as it stood (including inline party details); cancelling the amendment restores that snapshot, and submitting the amendment clears it.
claims.quote: Pre-amend snapshot of {@link #notification}. Amend-only scratchpad: captured when an amendment starts, restored by cancel-amend, and cleared when the amendment is submitted. Independent of {@link #preAmendFulfilments}; carries inline party details as they stood when the trader opened the amendment.

claims.statement: The fulfilments payload is snapshotted separately when an amendment starts, restored by cancelling the amendment and cleared when it is submitted, independently of the content snapshot.
claims.quote: Pre-amend snapshot of {@link #fulfilments}. Amend-only scratchpad: restored by cancel-amend and cleared when the amendment is submitted. Independent of the content freeze.

claims.statement: Neither pre-amendment snapshot is ever shown in a JSON response.
claims.quote:
@JsonIgnore
    private Notification preAmendNotification;

claims.statement: Wherever the backend needs a notification's content, a record with no content sub-object fails at once with an error rather than carrying on; the unexpected-error handler would turn that into a 500 response.
claims.quote:
return requireNonNull(notification,
            "NotificationAggregate requires a notification sub-object at this seam");
claims.note: Inferred that the failure reaches a caller as 500: a NullPointerException is a RuntimeException, which GlobalExceptionHandler.handleException maps to 500. Which endpoints reach this seam is parts 2 and 3.

claims.statement: A request to save a notification has a body with a notification object, which is required, and an optional actor object.
A save request without a notification object is rejected with a 400 validation error naming the notification field.
claims.quote:
@NotNull
    NotificationDto notification;
claims.note: Inferred from @NotNull together with the MethodArgumentNotValidException handler. NotificationController applies @Valid to the SaveNotificationDto body at lines 52 (POST /notifications) and 71 (PUT by reference number); which endpoints those are is parts 2 and 3. The message would be the Bean Validation default ("must not be null").

claims.statement: The actor on a save request identifies who made the change: an id, a source, a user type, a display name, an organisation id and the organisation id acted on behalf of; it is passed on as the actor of the change.
claims.note: ActorRequest is not in this part's read list; it was read because SaveNotificationDto names it. Where the actor goes (the outbox Actor) is part 5.

The request shape is only ever inbound: no endpoint returns it; every endpoint returns the stored notification or one of its view projections.
claims.quote: It is never a response body — every endpoint returns {@link NotificationAggregate} or one of the view projections

claims.statement: A date-only field sent as a date-time, such as 2026-07-21T00:00:00Z or 2026-07-21T00:00:00, is rejected with a 400 rather than having its time part silently dropped.
claims.quote: Jackson's {@code LocalDateDeserializer} is lenient by default: handed {@code 2026-07-21T00:00:00Z} or {@code 2026-07-21T00:00:00} it keeps the date part and drops the rest. A caller that sends a moment where a calendar date belongs would then be told 200, and the day it meant would depend on a zone nobody stated. With leniency off the value fails to parse and the caller gets 400.

claims.statement: The strict-date rule applies to every date-only field, including any added in future, because it is set for the date type rather than field by field; timestamp fields are not affected.
claims.quote: The override is set for the type rather than with {@code @JsonFormat} on each field, so a future {@code LocalDate} field cannot forget it. {@code Instant} binding is untouched.

claims.quote: expect(doc.status).toBe('SUBMITTED'); expect(notification.origin.countryCode).toBe('FR'); expect(notification.origin.requiresRegionCode).toBe('yes'); expect(notification.origin.regionOfOriginCode).toBe('FR-75'); expect(notification.origin.internalReference).toBe('Imports456GB');

claims.statement: The stored commodity has name Cow and a commodityComplement whose species carries text Bos taurus, the scalar earTag and an animalIdentifiers list in which an unanswered passport is stored as an empty string.
claims.quote: expect(notification.commodity.name).toBe('Cow'); expect(species.text).toBe('Bos taurus'); expect(species.earTag).toBe('UK123456789012'); expect(species.animalIdentifiers).toEqual([{ earTag: 'UK123456789012', passport: '' }]);

claims.statement: The stored commodity complement holds totalNoOfAnimals 1 and totalNoOfPackages 5.
claims.quote: expect(complement.totalNoOfAnimals).toBe(1); expect(complement.totalNoOfPackages).toBe(5);

claims.statement: The stored import reason is reasonForImport internalMarket with purposeInInternalMarket breeding, and additionalDetails holds certifiedFor slaughter and unweanedAnimals no.
claims.quote: expect(notification.reasonForImport).toBe('internalMarket'); expect(notification.purposeInInternalMarket).toBe('breeding'); expect(notification.additionalDetails.certifiedFor).toBe('slaughter'); expect(notification.additionalDetails.unweanedAnimals).toBe('no');

claims.statement: The stored party address has addressLine1, townOrCity, postcode and countryCode.
claims.quote: address: { addressLine1: consignor.addressLine1, townOrCity: consignor.townOrCity, postcode: consignor.postcode, countryCode: consignor.countryCode }

claims.statement: The consignment contact address is stored in the notification field consignment.
claims.quote: expect(notification.consignment).toMatchObject({ name: contact.name, address: { postcode: contact.postcode } });

claims.statement: A notification that has never been amended has no preAmendNotification snapshot stored.
claims.quote: expect(doc.preAmendNotification).toBeUndefined();
claims.note: Implies an amendment stores the submitted version as preAmendNotification so cancel-amend can restore it; no trace here reads that field.

claims.statement: The stored CPH number is the nine digits joined without separators (123456789).
claims.quote: expect(notification.cphNumber).toBe('123456789');

claims.statement: The stored transport holds portOfEntry GB ABD, meansOfTransport ROAD_VEHICLE, transportIdentification, transportDocumentReference, transitedCountries in the order added (FR, BE) and a transporter with name and type.
claims.quote: expect(notification.transport.portOfEntry).toBe('GB ABD'); expect(notification.transport.meansOfTransport).toBe('ROAD_VEHICLE'); ... expect(notification.transport.transitedCountries).toEqual(['FR', 'BE']); expect(notification.transport.transporter?.name).toBe('García Livestock Transport SL'); expect(notification.transport.transporter?.type).toBe('Commercial');

claims.statement: The arrival date is stored as a YYYY-MM-DD string of the chosen calendar date, so it cannot drift with the backend's timezone.
claims.quote: the stored value must be the chosen calendar date, whatever timezone the backend JVM runs in. It is stored as a `YYYY-MM-DD` string, which has no zone to drift in.

claims.statement: After submission the notification view reloads from storage as read-only with the Submitted status.
claims.quote: await expect(animalsPages.notificationView.journeyStrip).toContainText('Submitted');

claims.statement: A notification seeded through the frontend's form posts stores the same status, notification content and fulfilments as the same journey walked in the browser.
claims.quote: expect(seededDoc.status).toBe(browserDoc.status); expect(seededDoc.notification).toEqual(browserDoc.notification); expect(seededDoc.fulfilments).toEqual(browserDoc.fulfilments);
claims.note: In the trace the seeded notification (GBN-AG-26-Y17M0A) is created by POSTs to the frontend routes without a concurrency token, ending with the declaration; parity holds even though the seed skips the hub.

claims.statement: The seeded parity journey omits the empty passport field that the browser posts, yet the stored notifications still match.
claims.ref: trace animals-e2e-journeys-persi-d751b--stores-through-the-browser-animals network: browser POST /commodities/identification vs seeded POST

claims.statement: The Mongo document reads behind every persistence test are not recorded in the traces, so the stored shapes above rest on the spec assertions rather than captured documents.

claims.quote: Every party is a copy of the record picked for it, with no link back to the address book ... expect(notification.consignor).not.toHaveProperty('addressId'); ... expect(notification.destination).toMatchObject({ name: destination.name, address: { postcode: destination.postcode } });
